plain: Outer alignment asks whether the training goal is the right goal; inner alignment asks whether the trained model actually learned that goal.
eli5: Did we write the right rule, and did the robot really learn that rule or just something that looked like it?
technical: From Hubinger et al. (2019): outer alignment is whether the base objective is a good proxy for what we want (its failures include specification gaming), and inner alignment is whether a learned (mesa-) objective matches the base objective (its failures include goal misgeneralisation and deceptive alignment).
